89ebb234-da99-4e5b-ae43-e2739b386925.title: EAP 1: Functional Boundaries and Organisational Flexibility
89ebb234-da99-4e5b-ae43-e2739b386925.principle:
### Statement
To achieve clear functional boundaries, **Draftsman products are designed as separate systems**.

### Rationale
This separation provides **organisational flexibility**, allowing each product to evolve independently — both technically and legally.
For example, we can use separate legal entities ("rechtsvormen") for different products, enabling isolation where needed.

### Implication / Acceptance
We accept that this design prevents us from **bundling our software** (e.g. *“pay once and access both Tracepaper and Workbench”*).
Each product must therefore justify its own value proposition and pricing model.

a201f648-b359-4621-b45c-8ea40b4d76e3.title: EAP 2: We prefere serverless technologies
a201f648-b359-4621-b45c-8ea40b4d76e3.principle:
### Statement
To ensure scalability and reduce operational overhead, **we prefer serverless technologies** over self-managed infrastructure.  
This principle guides our architectural choices toward services that automatically scale and minimize maintenance effort.

### Rationale
Serverless platforms allow teams to focus on business logic instead of infrastructure management.  
They support **cost efficiency**, **automatic scaling**, and **fine-grained billing**, aligning with our goal of lean, adaptive systems.  
While serverless imposes vendor constraints, its benefits in speed and autonomy outweigh those trade-offs for most workloads.

### Implication / Acceptance
We accept that this preference limits our ability to deploy in certain on-premise or multi-cloud environments.  
Teams choosing non-serverless options must explicitly justify their decision and document how operational risks are mitigated.
